'''Jack M. Wilson''' (born 1945) is an [[Americans|American]] [[educator]],  [[entrepreneur]] and the President-Emeritus and Distinguished Professor of Higher Education, Emerging Technologies, and Innovation at the [[University of Massachusetts]] Lowell. During his career, he has served various institutions as [[professor]] of [[physics]], [[Academic department|department]] chair, [[research center]] director, [[Dean (education)|dean]], [[Provost (education)|provost]], vice president, and [[Chancellor (education)#University president|president]], and has served with multiple [[professional societies]] and government committees.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.uml.edu/MSB/faculty/Wilson-Jack.aspx|title=Jack Wilson {{!}} Faculty & Staff {{!}} Manning School of Business {{!}} UMass Lowell|website=www.uml.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref>

== Education and early life ==
Wilson earned his bachelor's degree at [[Thiel College]] in 1967.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thiel.edu/alumni/awards|title=Alumni Awards {{!}} Thiel College|website=www.thiel.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref> His master's degree (1970) and doctorate (1972) in physics were both earned from [[Kent State University]].<ref name="About" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kent.edu/physics/ksu-phd-physics-alumni|title=KSU Ph.D. Physics Alumni {{!}} Physics {{!}} Kent State University|website=www.kent.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04|archive-date=2018-10-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004151311/https://www.kent.edu/physics/ksu-phd-physics-alumni|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2004 Wilson received an honorary doctorate degree from Thiel College.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thiel.edu/about/honorary-degree-recipients|title=Honorary Degree Recipients {{!}} Thiel College|website=www.thiel.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref>

==Career==

===Professor and administrator===
Wilson began his professional career in physics as an instructor at [[Kent State University]] in Ohio.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://omeka.library.kent.edu/special-collections/items/show/198|title=Wilson, Jack · Kent State University Libraries. Special Collections and Archives|website=omeka.library.kent.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref> He then moved to the physics department at [[Sam Houston State University]] in Texas. In his ten years there (1972–82) he was first professor, then department chair, and eventually director of their Division of Chemistry, Physics, and Physical Sciences.<ref name="Vita">{{cite web|url=http://www.jackmwilson.net/WilsonVitaFrame.htm|title=Vita|last=Wilson|first=Jack M.|work=Jack M. Wilson, Ph.D.|publisher=www.JackMWilson.net}}</ref>

After two years as guest scientist at the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]] (1982–84) and Executive Officer of the American Association of Physics Teachers (AAPT), Wilson moved to the University of Maryland. From 1984 to 1990, he was a professor of physics at the [[University of Maryland]]'s main campus<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physics.umd.edu/rgroups/ripe/muppet/muppet.html|title=The M.U.P.P.E.T. Utilities -- Programming tools for solving physics problems|website=www.physics.umd.edu|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref> and continued as the Executive Officer of AAPT.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.aapt.org/olympiad2000/about.html|title=American Association of Physics Teachers}}</ref> He also served as Co-Director of the Maryland University Project in Physics and Educational Technology.<ref name=Vita/>

In January 1990, Wilson resigned from AAPT<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aapt.org/aboutaapt/history/execoffice.cfm|title=Executive Office|website=www.aapt.org|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref> and went to [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] in New York, as director of the Lois J. and Harlan E. Anderson Center for Innovation in Undergraduate Education and Professor of Physics. In 1997 he was appointed as the J. Erik Jonsson '22 Distinguished Professor of Physics, Engineering Science, Information Technology, and Management at RPI, a capacity he held until 2001. He also served RPI as a Dean, Research Center Director, and interim Provost.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archives.rpi.edu/jack-m-wilson-dean-of-facultyprovost-acting-1997-2000/|title=Rensselaer - Entry about Jack M. Wilson, Dean of Faculty / Provost}}</ref> He was also chairman of the board for RPI's extension campus, [[Rensselaer at Hartford]].<ref name=Vita/>

====University of Massachusetts====

=====UMassOnline=====
Wilson founded [[UMassOnline]] in 2001, which enables students to earn accredited degrees online from the UMass system. From 2001 to 2003, he served as CEO. As the CEO of UMassOnline, he helped to build the system-wide initiative into one of the largest externally directed online programs in the United States, with 64 graduate and undergraduate degree and certificate programs serving more than 64,000 enrollees in 2014 with revenues of over $85 million for the university. For his work in "advancing the quality and scale of online and blended education", he was named to the Online Learning Consortiums (OLC) 2015 class of fellows.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.umassonline.net/2015/12/08-Congratulations-To-UMassOnline-Founder-Jack-Wilson|title=Congratulations to UMassOnline Founder Jack Wilson! {{!}} www.umassonline.net|website=www.umassonline.net|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref>

=====University president=====
At the University of Massachusetts, he first served as the Vice President for Academic Affairs in 2003.

Wilson served as the 25th President of the [[University of Massachusetts]] system, from 2003 to 2011, overseeing their five campuses and 60,000 students.<ref name=About /> Wilson is now the President Emeritus of the UMass system.<ref name=":0" />

At the University of Massachusetts, Wilson called for a rededication to the [[Land-grant university|land grant]] mission as it might be viewed in the context of a modern innovative society. He believed that UMass played a critical role in Massachusetts, saying "The path to economic and social development in Massachusetts goes through the University of Massachusetts."<ref name=Net>{{cite web | url = http://www.jackmwilson.net | title = Jack M. Wilson, Ph.D. | publisher = www.JackMWilson.net }}</ref>

Wilson believed that financial aid is the key to affordability and accessibility. He increased financial aid by 267% during his eight-year term at a time when financial aid from other sources was not growing substantially. He also established a scholarship fund with the proceeds of an insurance policy; at the time of his retirement as president in 2011, additional donations had brought the total fund to $2.1 million.<ref name="scholarship">{{cite news | url = http://www.bizjournals.com/boston/news/2011/06/02/umass-president-funds-scholarship.html | title = UMass Prez Wilson chips in for $2.1M scholarship fund in his own name | date = June 2, 2011 | first = Mary | last = Moore | work = Boston Business Journal}}</ref>

Recognizing that the university needed investment in infrastructure, he restructured the UMass Building Authority and launched a building program. UMass made $1.6 billion in capital investments in the first five years of his presidential term and established a capital program of $2.9 billion more to be carried out over the next decade.

He created Presidential grant programs to encourage the growth of research and the creative economy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.umassonline.net/Jack-Wilson-Presidential-Scholarship|title=Jack M. Wilson Presidential Scholarship Fund {{!}} www.umassonline.net|website=www.umassonline.net|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref>  During his eight years as president, research at the university increased by 69% and the commercialization of the intellectual property generated by that research increased by 105%.<ref name="Boston Globe">{{cite news | url = http://archive.boston.com/business/articles/2011/02/10/umass_research_funding_reaches_record/ | title = UMass research funding reaches record | first = D.C. | last = Denison | date = February 10, 2011 | work = Boston Globe}}</ref>  This put UMass at eighth in the nation at the time of his departure in 2011, according to the ranking of the Association of University Technology Managers.
Wilson also established international programs as a major priority and recruited the first Vice President to carry the title "International Relations" as part of her title. He identified Africa, Japan, China, Germany, India, and the Portuguese language countries as particular first targets of opportunity, building on existing relationships of the university and his own work.

=====Other UMass initiatives=====
He served as the Founding Chair of the [[Massachusetts Green High Performance Computing Center]]. The Center is a joint venture among UMass, MIT, Harvard, Boston University, and Northeastern with support from EMC, Cisco, Accenture, and other companies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mghpcc.org/ceremonial-ground-breaking/|title=Massachusetts Green High Performance Computing Center: Ceremonial Ground Breaking|date=5 October 2010 }}</ref>

During the academic year 2012–13, he served as the interim Dean of Engineering at [[UMass Lowell]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uml.edu/News/press-releases/2012/IndustryDay111412.aspx|title=UMass Lowell Industry Day Salutes Partnerships {{!}} UMass Lowell|website=www.uml.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04|archive-date=2012-11-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121123023143/http://www.uml.edu/News/press-releases/2012/IndustryDay111412.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref> He continues at UMass Lowell as University Distinguished Professor of Higher Education, Innovation, and Emerging Technologies.<ref name=":0" />

===Entrepreneur===
In the [[private sector]], Wilson was the founder, CEO, and Chairman of the LearnLinc Corporation, founded in 1993 as a spin-off of his university research. After several mergers he formed the [[Public company|publicly traded]] Mentergy Corporation, leaving the company in the next year.  Following the formation of Mentergy through a triple reverse merger with Gilat Communications, John Bryce Training and Allen Communications in early 2001, the company's market value on [[NASDAQ]] was around $500 million.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.czechleaders.com/interviews/jack-wilson|title=Jack Wilson - Czech & Slovak Leaders|date=2017-09-12|work=Czech & Slovak Leaders|access-date=2018-10-04|language=en-GB}}</ref>

He has served as a consultant to many computing and communications firms. Clients include IBM, AT&T, Lucent, Hewlett Packard, and Boeing Flight Safety International.<ref name="Vita" /><ref name="About" />

Wilson's expertise in building links between higher education, government, and business led to co-founding RPI's [[Lally School of Management & Technology#Severino Center for Technological Entrepreneurship|Severino Center for Technological Entrepreneurship]] as well as other programs.

==Further affiliations==
From 1982 to 1990, Wilson served as the head of the [[American Association of Physics Teachers]], a scientific society in Washington, DC.<ref name=Vita/><ref name=":1" /> He also served as an officer of the American Institute of Physics<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/collections/executive-committee/october-1-1989|title=October 1, 1989|date=2015-10-23|access-date=2018-10-04|language=en}}</ref> and the Chairman of the American Physical Society,<ref name="About">{{cite web|title=About the President: Jack M. Wilson PhD|url=http://www.massachusetts.edu/po/aboutjmw.html|publisher=[[University of Massachusetts]]|date=March 1, 2010|accessdate=17 January 2011| archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20100818135451/http://www.massachusetts.edu/po/aboutjmw.html | archivedate = August 18, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/units/fed/newsletters/upload/spring02.pdf|title=American Physical Society - Chair Wilson speaking at 2002 Spring Forum on Education}}</ref> and is a Fellow of both.

He was appointed to the U.S. [[Education Commission of the States]] in 2005 by Massachusetts Governor Mitt Romney and then reappointed in 2010 by Governor Deval Patrick. In 2011,<ref name=Net-FBI>{{cite web | url = http://www.jackmwilson.net/FBI.html | title = Federal Bureau of Investigation | work = Jack M. Wilson, Ph.D. | publisher = www.JackMWilson.net}}</ref> the FBI honored him for his service on the National Security Higher Education Advisory Board.

He has also served as a member or chair of several study committees and task forces for the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and the Academy's National Research Council.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sites.nationalacademies.org/pga/guirr/PGA_050841|title=University Industry Partners Membership List|last=PGA|website=sites.nationalacademies.org|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ecs.org/wp-content/uploads/AnnualReport2010.pdf|title=2010 Annual Report: Education Commission of the States}}</ref>

He also served on the [[Edward M. Kennedy Institute for the United States Senate]]. He was a member of the Board of Directors and then was interim President from 2011 to 2012.

He served as the Chair of the US Department of Education Fund for the Improvement of Post-Secondary Education (FIPSE) Advisory Board from 2010 to 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ed.gov/news/press-releases/us-secretary-education-announces-new-board-members-fund-improvement-postsecondar|title=U.S. Secretary of Education Announces New Board Members for Fund for the Improvement of Postsecondary Education {{!}} U.S. Department of Education|website=www.ed.gov|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04}}</ref>

He is presently serving on the board of the Advanced Cyber Security Center.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acscenter.org/news/news_details.html?id=428|title=Advance Cyber Security Center|website=www.acscenter.org|language=en|access-date=2018-10-04|archive-date=2018-10-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004185743/https://www.acscenter.org/news/news_details.html?id=428|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He chairs the Investment Advisory Committee of the Innovation Institute for the Massachusetts Technology Collaborative.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://masstech.org/sites/mtc/files/documents/AR2015_web.pdf|title=Massachusetts Technology Collaborative - 2015 Annual Report|access-date=2018-10-04|archive-date=2016-12-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220185950/http://masstech.org/sites/mtc/files/documents/AR2015_web.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Awards==
Wilson has won multiple awards for his leadership in the reform of higher education programs and his innovative programs.

*[[TIAA–CREF]]: Theodore Hesburgh Award for Innovation in Undergraduate Education, 1995
*[[Boeing]] Corporation: The Boeing Outstanding Educator Award, 1995
*[[The Pew Charitable Trusts]]:  The Pew Charitable Trust Award for Outstanding Achievement in Undergraduate Education, 1996
*United States Army: Outstanding Civilian Service Medal for service to the Army Education program, 2001
*Massachusetts Alliance for Economic Development: Statewide Strategic Asset award, 2004
*''Mass High Tech Magazine'': Massachusetts All Star, 2005
*Knox Trail Council of the [[Boy Scouts of America]]: Westborough Good Scout Award, November 2010<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.massachusetts.edu/news/press-releases/president-wilson-honored-scouts|title=President Wilson honored by Scouts|date=2014-11-12|work=University of Massachusetts|access-date=2018-10-04|language=en|archive-date=2018-10-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004145045/https://www.massachusetts.edu/news/press-releases/president-wilson-honored-scouts|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*Massachusetts Technology Leadership Council: Workforce Development Leader of the Year, 2010<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.masstlc.org/masstlc-leadership-award-winners-2010/|title=MassTLC Leadership Award Winners 2010 {{!}} MassTLC|date=2010-09-15|work=MassTLC|access-date=2018-10-04|language=en-US}}</ref>
*FBI/Department of Justice: Exceptional Service in the Public Interest, 2011<ref name=Net-FBI/>

==Personal life==
Wilson lives in Bradenton, Florida. He is married, the father of four children, and grandfather of five.<ref name="About" />
